input: Gou et al. (2024) report that iterative correction in CRITIC generally improves results, with a notable surge when only erroneous samples are modified (an oracle setting), and that the marginal benefit of more corrections diminishes, with 2-3 rounds giving most of the gain. Critique a claim that more correction rounds always help and that the oracle-setting numbers describe realistic deployment.
source: Gou et al. 2024, Section 4.4 Additional Ablations and Analysis (chunk gou2024-026)
